origin.description: Foster, Greer, and Thorbecke poverty index for an income vector at an absolute poverty line.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: Income vector. The index is defined for non-negative values.

arguments.name: k
arguments.text: Absolute poverty line, a single constant.

arguments.name: parameter
arguments.text: Sensitivity of the index. NULL uses 1. The value 1 is the headcount ratio and 2 is the poverty gap ratio.

arguments.name: na.rm
arguments.text: If true, drop missing values before computing. If false, any missing value makes the result missing.

origin.details: Only incomes strictly below the line enter the sum. Parameter 1 counts those people, which is the headcount ratio. Parameter 2 averages their shortfall over the whole sample, which is the poverty gap ratio. A NULL parameter uses 1. When nobody is strictly below the line, the index is 0.
origin.value: A single number, the Foster index.
origin.example:
# generate vectors (of incomes)
x <- c(541, 1463, 2445, 3438, 4437, 5401, 6392, 8304, 11904, 22261)
y <- c(841, 2063, 2445, 3438, 4437, 5401, 6392, 8304, 11304, 21961)
# compute Watts index with poverty line 2000
pov(x, 2000)
pov(y, 2000)
# compute headcount ratio with poverty line 2000
pov(x, 2000, parameter=1, type="Foster")
pov(y, 2000, parameter=1, type="Foster")

translation.description: Foster, Greer, and Thorbecke poverty index for an income vector at an absolute poverty line.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: Income vector. The index is defined for non-negative values. Missing values are NaN.

arguments.name: k
arguments.text: Absolute poverty line, a single constant.

arguments.name: parameter
arguments.text: Sensitivity of the index. None uses 1. The value 1 is the headcount ratio and 2 is the poverty gap ratio.

arguments.name: na_rm
arguments.text: If true, drop missing values before computing. If false, any missing value makes the result NaN.

translation.details: Each income strictly below the line contributes ((line - income) / line) raised to parameter - 1, and the sum is divided by the sample length. None uses 1, so the headcount ratio is the default and parameter 2 is the poverty gap ratio. pov() passes parameter through, so None matches Foster's own default. When nobody is strictly below the line, the index is 0.
translation.value: A single number, the Foster index.
translation.example:
from ineq.poverty import pov

# generate vectors (of incomes)
x = [541, 1463, 2445, 3438, 4437, 5401, 6392, 8304, 11904, 22261]
y = [841, 2063, 2445, 3438, 4437, 5401, 6392, 8304, 11304, 21961]
# compute Watts index with poverty line 2000
print(pov(x, 2000))
print(pov(y, 2000))
# compute headcount ratio with poverty line 2000
print(pov(x, 2000, parameter=1, type="Foster"))
print(pov(y, 2000, parameter=1, type="Foster"))
